These books are a value and treasure greater than a college education in comparative mythology and religious studies ever could be. Give yourself the keys of discernment. Listen to Spirit Whirled.

recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements—the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Name: LotusWei Flower Elixirs
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Offer Line: Use my affiliate link to support InnerVerse

recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Body: George Wiseman is the inventor of the AquaCure AC50 and founder of Eagle Research, where he has spent decades developing hydrogen and oxygen (Brown's gas) technology for health and home use. He has appeared on InnerVerse multiple times to talk about hydrogen as a macronutrient and EZ water.
recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Name: AquaCure AC50
recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" for a discount

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

recyrScE8pr74frbJ.Bio: Katie Hess is the founder of LotusWei and author of Flowerevolution, known for her work crafting flower and plant essence elixirs; she discussed the history and symbolism of flower essence medicine on InnerVerse.
recyrScE8pr74frbJ.Name: Katie Hess

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Why yarrow ended up in everything", "body": "Kyle Denton opens on yarrow, the plant he maps to February 8th in Aquarius, describing it in Thomsonian terms as a regulator of circulation and noting that distilling it draws out azulene, the compound that turns the hydrosol sky blue. Katie Hess explains why LOTUSWEI now puts yarrow in every product: a post Fukushima trip where every person in Tokyo taking her iPad flower quiz chose white yarrow, then a slow surge at American farmers markets she reads as a response to daily EMF exposure. Michelle Lundquist adds the umbel connection, seeing wild carrot, Angelica and yarrow as firmament symbolism, each floret a star."}, {"title": "Mapping plants onto the zodiac wheel", "body": "Denton describes placing plants at specific degrees on the astrological calendar wheel, a system he and Lundquist built out with Chance Garton and a couple of symbolism experts across a year long InnerVerse series covering all twelve signs and the doctrine of signatures. He uses Gemini season as the example: the paired organs, the two lungs, breath and speech, with the neck as Taurus and the head as Aries on the zodiacal man. Lundquist says their Astro herbs crew deliberately pushed past the standard planetary correspondences toward color, shape and organ systems, and that her own current obsession is mugwort under a venusian rather than lunar correspondence."}, {"title": "Going to the plant instead of the book", "body": "Hess says she avoids books about flower essences entirely and goes straight to the source, asking the Earth to describe a flower in the words the people she will reach need to hear. She argues four people collecting the same dandelion would each receive different language, shaped by their own community and its needs, and she cites Stephen Harrod Buhner on plants altering their constituents in response to a request. Denton describes the same turn in his herbalism, calling books training wheels he stopped appealing to once a teacher taught him to read plants through the senses. He credits a grape vine with a thought about starting a men's group."}, {"title": "Fractals, ripples and the fear remedies", "body": "Lundquist raises the fractal and toroidal nature of flowers and people, suggesting essences let us tap deeper into that self similar pattern. Hess reframes it as ripple effect, citing a client whose whole family shifted after seven years, her first teacher's claim that three percent of the population on these remedies could change the planet's outcome, and a ten year happiness study where a friend of a friend of a friend becoming wildly happy beat fifty five thousand dollars in cash. Garton reports the same pattern in biofield tuning, where estranged relatives call within the week, and says a Lotus Wei elixir handed him a session's theme up front."}, {"title": "Japanese camellia and the hunger for order", "body": "Hess brings the panel a live puzzle: for about eight months nearly everyone taking her flower quiz has chosen Japanese camellia, which she associates with a heart hardened by disappointment. Lundquist points to financial insecurity and a slow drip collapse people sense coming, and offers the oxeye daisy from her bouquet as a stand in your center flower, a sync Denton confirms after sitting with the same plant while scouting a Sunday herb walk. He also rejects the label invasive, citing a listener's usage map dating the term to roughly 1995 and calling it marketing. A closing tea round lands on rose thorns, chamomile and ceremonial cacao."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Our new friend Katie Hess of LOTUSWEI joins Vibe Rant to mix it up with our herbalist regulars, Kyle Denton (Tippecanoe Herbs) and Michelle Lundquist (Michelle's Healing Home). We'll let this meeting of the minds play out with its own organic flow, but expect to learn about making flower essences and their gentle yet transformative effects. Flower Power, ya'll!
